content.title: Alec Baldwin plans retirement after Rust ordeal and health decline
content.text: Baldwin discloses health collapse, announces retirement In interviews with The Hollywood Reporter and multiple podcasts, Baldwin said he wants to retire after nearly five decades in acting, citing the toll of the Rust tragedy. He revealed he had been diagnosed with orthostatic hypotension, suffered blackouts, and spent over a week bedridden during litigation. Baldwin said he grew accustomed to being home with his seven young children and no longer wishes to leave for work. Daily Mail + 2 "I blacked out three times during the St. Patrick's Day weekend of that year, and fell on top of my wife once. It was crazy. It was horrible. So I get into bed. I'm in bed for eight days. I can't get out of bed. I can't walk. I had to go to physical therapy for two weeks."Alec Baldwin A career and health shaped by 'Rust' fallout The 2021 fatal shooting of Halyna Hutchins on the Rust set triggered years of legal battles and personal strain for Baldwin. He described the experience as 'very painful', impacting his finances, career trajectory, and mental health. His wife, Hilaria, publicly addressed his PTSD and declining wellbeing, while Baldwin admitted to periods of deep depression and thoughts of suicide. The Independent + 1 From on-set tragedy to legal battles Baldwin faced involuntary manslaughter charges, which were dismissed in 2024 after prosecutors withdrew their appeal. He accused New Mexico prosecutors of misconduct and seeking publicity, while noting that evidence was allegedly hidden during the trial. The settlement with Hutchins’ widower required Baldwin to complete Rust, which he did despite illness, in order to avoid further legal action. The Independent + 2 What Baldwin's retirement means for Hollywood Baldwin’s potential retirement marks the end of an era for a prolific actor whose career spanned nearly 50 years. His decision underscores the lasting personal and professional repercussions of high-profile on-set accidents in Hollywood. The Rust case has already influenced industry discussions on set safety, legal accountability, and the mental health of those involved in such tragedies. Daily Mail + 1 3 references
